questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
$7.9\text{ MeV } \alpha\text{-particle}$ scatters from a target material of atomic number $79$. From the given data the estimated diameter of nuclei of the target material is (approximately) \_
\_\_ $\text{m}$.
$$\left[\frac{1}{4\pi \epsilon_0} = 9\times 10^9 \text{ Nm}^2 / \text{C}^2 \text{and electron charge} = 1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{C}\right]$$
questions.solution: Sol. By mechanical energy conservation Figure showing an $\alpha$ particle with charge $q_1 = 2e$ moving towards a target material with charge $q_2 = Ze$, represented by a dashed circle. $(\text{Me})_i = (\text{Me})_f$ $\text{PE}_i + \text{KE}_i = \text{PE}_f + \text{KE}_f$ $0 + 7.9 \times 10^6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = \frac{\text{k}(2\text{e})(Ze)}{\text{r}} + 0$ $\text{r} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2 \times \left(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)^2 \times 79}{7.9 \times 10^6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 2.88 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}$ For diameter $\Rightarrow \text{D} = 2\text{r} = 5.76 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}$

questions.text: The escape velocity from a spherical planet A is $10\text{ km/s}$. The escape velocity from another planet B whose density and radius are $10\%$ of those of planet A, is $\rule{1cm}{0.15mm}\text{ m/s}$.
questions.solution:
Sol. $V_{\text{e}} = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{\frac{}{\text{R}}} \Rightarrow V_{\text{e}} \propto \sqrt{\rho} \times \text{R}$

$\frac{(V_{\text{e}})_{\text{B}}}{(V_{\text{e}})_{\text{A}}} = \sqrt{\frac{\rho_{\text{B}}}{\rho_{\text{A}}}} \times \frac{\text{R}_{\text{B}}}{\text{R}_{\text{A}}} = \sqrt{\frac{0.1\rho_{\text{A}}}{\rho_{\text{A}}}} \times \left(\frac{0.1\text{R}_{\text{A}}}{\text{R}_{\text{A}}}\right)$

$\frac{(V_{\text{e}})_{\text{B}}}{(V_{\text{e}})_{\text{A}}} = \frac{1}{10} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

$(V_{\text{e}})_{\text{B}} = \frac{10 \times 1000}{10\sqrt{10}} = 100\sqrt{10}\text{m} / \text{sec}$

questions.text: A meter bridge with two resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ as shown in figure was balanced (null point) at $40\text{ cm}$ from the point P. The null point changed to $50\text{ cm}$ from the point P, when $16\;\Omega$ resistance is connected in parallel to $R_2$. The values of resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ are $\text{\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_}$.
questions.solution: Sol. Circuit diagram 1 shows two loops with resistors $R_1$ and $R_2$ and respective lengths 40 and 60. Circuit diagram 2 shows two loops with resistors $R_1$ and $R_2$, lengths 50 and 50, and a resistor of $16\,\Omega$ connected in parallel with $R_2$. $$\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3} \quad \quad \dots\dots (1)$$ $$\frac{R_1}{\left(\frac{R_2 \times 16}{R_2 + 16}\right)} = \frac{50}{50} \Rightarrow R_1 = \frac{16R_2}{16 + R_2} \quad \dots\dots (2)$$ $$\frac{2}{3}R_2 = \frac{16R_2}{16 + R_2}$$ $$\frac{32}{3} + \frac{2R_2}{3} = 16$$ $$\frac{2R_2}{3} = 16 - \frac{32}{3} = \frac{16}{3}$$ $$R_2 = 8\,\Omega$$ By equation (1) $$R_1 = \frac{2}{3}R_2 = \frac{16}{3}\,\Omega$$

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I :** Pressure of fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid.

**Statement II:** Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to interior, results in surface tension.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: Sol. According to pascal's law pressure at any point in liquid at rest is same in all direction. It exist at every point in the liquid not just at boundaries. So statement (1) is false. For interior molecule net cohesive forces are zero statement (2) is correct.

questions.text: Net gravitational force at the centre of a square is found to be $F_1$ when four particles having mass $M$, $2M$, $3M$ and $4M$ are placed at the four corners of the square as shown in figure and it is $F_2$ when the positions of $3M$ and $4M$ are interchanged. The ratio $\frac{F_1}{F_2}$ is $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{5}}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.solution: Sol. Initial configuration A rectangle of side $L$ with masses $m$, $3m$, $4m$, and $2m$ at its four corners, and mass $m_0$ at the intersection of diagonals. Force vectors are shown directed along the diagonals towards the corners: $\frac{Gm m_0}{r^2}$, $\frac{G4 m m_0}{r^2}$, $\frac{G3 m m_0}{r^2}$, and $\frac{G2 m m_0}{r^2}$. A simplified vector diagram shows the net components. $$F = 2\sqrt{2}\frac{Gmm_0}{r^2}$$ New configuration The masses at the top-left and top-right are swapped ($3m$ and $4m$). Force vectors are updated accordingly on the rectangle and in the simplified vector diagram. $$F' = \sqrt{10}\frac{Gmm_0}{r^2} \Rightarrow \frac{F}{F'} = 2\sqrt{2}.\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$$ $$\therefore \alpha = 2$$

questions.text: A cylindrical tube $AB$ of length $l$, closed at both ends contains an ideal gas of $1\text{ mol}$ having molecular weight $M$. The tube is rotated in a horizontal plane with constant angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis perpendicular to $AB$ and passing through the edge at end A, as shown in the figure. If $P_A$ and $P_B$ are the pressures at $A$ and $B$ respectively, then (Consider the temperature is same at all points in the tube)
questions.solution: Sol. Figure shows a horizontal tube containing a fluid, with a small element of thickness $\mathrm{dx}$ at distance $x$ from one end. The acceleration is $a_c = \omega^2 x$. Forces on the element are $P$ from the left and $(P + dP)$ from the right. $A[(P + dP) - P] = (\mathrm{dm})(\omega^2 x)$ $\mathrm{dP} = \frac{(\mathrm{dm})}{\mathrm{A}} \omega^2 x$ $\mathrm{dP} = \frac{(\rho)(\mathrm{A})(\mathrm{dx})\omega^2 x}{\mathrm{A}}$ also $[\mathrm{PM} = \rho\mathrm{RT}]$ $\rho = \frac{\mathrm{PM}}{\mathrm{RT}}$ $\mathrm{dP} = \left(\frac{\mathrm{PM}}{\mathrm{RT}}\right)\omega^2 x\mathrm{dx}$ $\int_{\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{A}}^{\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{B}} \frac{\mathrm{dP}}{\mathrm{P}} = \frac{\omega^2\mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{RT}}\int_{0}^{\ell} x\mathrm{dx}$ $\ell n \left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{B}}{\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{A}}\right) = \frac{\omega^2\ell^2\mathrm{M}}{2\mathrm{RT}}$ $\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{P}_\mathrm{A} \mathrm{e}^{\frac{\mathrm{M}\omega^2\ell^2}{2\mathrm{RT}}}$

questions.text: Rods x and y of equal dimensions but of different materials are joined as shown in figure. Temperatures of end points $A$ and $F$ are maintained at $100\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $40\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ respectively. Given the thermal conductivity of rod x is three times of that of rod y, the temperature at junction points $B$ and $E$ are (close to) :
questions.solution: Sol. Let $\left[\mathrm{R}=\frac{\ell}{3\mathrm{KA}}\right]$ Circuit diagram showing a resistor $R$ connected between node $T_A = 100$ and node $T_B$. From node $T_B$, the circuit splits into two parallel branches to node $T_E$: the upper branch contains two resistors of resistance $3R$ in series, and the lower branch contains two resistors of resistance $R$ in series. From node $T_E$, a resistor of resistance $3R$ connects to node $T_F = 40$. Equivalent circuit diagram showing a single resistor of resistance $11R/2$ connected between $T_A = 100$ and $T_F = 40$. $$\left[\mathrm{H} = \frac{100 - 40}{\dfrac{11\mathrm{R}}{2}}\right] \dots (1)$$ $$\mathrm{H} = \frac{100 - \mathrm{T_B}}{\mathrm{R}} \dots\dots (2)$$ $$\mathrm{H} = \frac{\mathrm{T_E} - 40}{3\mathrm{R}} \dots\dots (3)$$ using (1) and (2) $$120 = 1100 - 11\mathrm{T_A}$$ $\mathrm{T_B} = 89^\circ\mathrm{C}$ using (1) and (3) $\mathrm{T_E} = 73^\circ\mathrm{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider an equilateral prism (refractive index $\sqrt{2}$). A ray of light is incident on its one surface at a certain angle $i$. If the emergent ray is found to graze along the other surface then the angle of refraction at the incident surface is close to ____.
questions.solution: Sol. Equilateral prism. $A = 60^{\circ}$ A diagram showing an equilateral prism with angle $A$ at the apex. A ray of light enters the first refracting surface, refracting at angle $r_1$ with respect to the normal. It strikes the second surface at angle $r_2$ and emerges grazing the surface with angle of emergence $e = \pi/2$. $\mu \text{Sin} r_2 = 1. \text{sin} e = 1$ $\text{Sin} r_2 = \frac{1}{\mu} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $r_2 = 45^{\circ}$ $\therefore r_1 = A - r_2 = 15^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The volume of an ideal gas increases $8$ times and temperature becomes $(1/4)^{\text{th}}$ of initial temperature during a reversible change. If there is no exchange of heat in this process $(\Delta \text{Q} = 0)$ then identify the gas from the following options (Assuming the gases given in the options are ideal gases) :
questions.solution: Sol. $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$ $TV^{\gamma-1} = \text{constant}$ $TV^{\gamma-1} = \left(\frac{T}{4}\right)(8V)^{(\gamma-1)}$ $4 = 8^{(\gamma-1)}$ $2^{2} = 2^{3\gamma-3}$ $2 = 3(\gamma-1)$ $\gamma = \frac{5}{3}$ Gas is a monoatomic gas Answer is $\text{He}$..

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Electric field in a region is given by $\vec{E} = Axi\hat{} + By\hat{j}$, where $A = 10\text{ V/m}^2$ and $B = 5\text{ V/m}^2$. If the electric potential at a point $(10, 20)$ is $500\text{ V}$, then the electric potential at origin is $\rule{1cm}{0.15mm}\text{ V}$.
questions.solution: Sol. $\vec{\text{E}} = 10x\hat{\text{i}} + 5y\hat{\text{j}}$ $V_{\text{at } (10, 20)} = 500\text{ V}$ $\Delta \text{V} - \int \vec{\text{E}} \cdot \text{d}\vec{\text{r}}$ $500 - \text{V}_0 = -\int\limits_{(0,0)}^{(10,20)} (10x\hat{\text{i}} + 5y\hat{\text{j}}) \cdot (dx\hat{\text{i}} + dy\hat{\text{j}})$ $500 - \text{V}_0 = -\left[5x^2 + \frac{5y^2}{2}\right]_{(0,0)}^{(10,20)}$ $\text{V}_0 - 500 = \left(500 + 5 \times \frac{400}{2}\right) - (0 - 0)$ $\text{V}_0 - 500 = 500 + 1000$ $\text{V}_0 = 2000\text{ V}$

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

List-I List-II
A. Spring constant I. $\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-2}\text{K}^{-1}$
B. Thermal conductivity II. $\text{ML}^{0}\text{T}^{-2}$
C. Boltzmann constant III. $\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-2}$
D. Inductive reactance IV. $\text{MLT}^{-3}\text{K}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
Sol. (A) $F = Kx$
$[MLT^{-2}] = [K][L]$

(B) Thermal conductivity

An induced current flows through $\text{C}_2$ will be in clockwise direction when
options: $\text{C}_1$ and $\text{C}_3$ move with equal speeds away from $\text{C}_2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two loudspeakers ($L_1$ and $L_2$) are placed with a separation of $10\text{ m}$, as shown in figure. Both speakers are fed with an audio input signal of same frequency with constant volume. A voice recorder, initially at point $A$, at equidistance to both loud speakers, is moved by $25\text{ m}$ along the line $AB$ while monitoring the audio signal. The measured signal was found to undergo $10$ cycles of minima and maxima during the movement. The frequency of the input signal is $\rule{1cm}{0.15mm}$ $\text{Hz}$ $(\text{Speed of sound in air is } 324\text{ m/s and } \sqrt{5} = 2.23)$
questions.solution: Sol. Figure shows two sources $L_1$ and $L_2$ separated by a vertical distance with a horizontal separation of $40\text{ m}$. Point A is at a distance of $5\text{ m}$ from $L_2$ level, and point B is further up. The vertical distance from $L_1$ to B is $20\text{ m}$ (with a total distance of $25\text{ m}$ marked from A to B), and $L_2$ is $10\text{ m}$ below the level of A. Point B will $10^{\text{th}}$ maxima $\Delta \text{x} = \text{L}_2\text{B} - \text{L}_1\text{B}$ $\text{L}_1\text{B} = \sqrt{20^2 + 40^2} = 20\sqrt{5}\text{m} = 44.6\text{m}$ $\text{L}_2\text{B} = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = 50\text{m}$ $\Delta \text{x} = 50 - 44.6 = 5.4\text{ m}$ $\Delta \text{x} = \text{n}\lambda$ $5.4 = 10 \times \lambda$ $\lambda = 0.54\text{ m}$ $\text{V} = \text{f}\lambda$ $\text{f} = \frac{324}{0.54} = 600\text{Hz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave,
travelling in an unknown non-magnetic medium is
given by,
$E_y = 20 \sin (3 \times 10^6 x - 4.5 \times 10^{14} t) \text{ V/m}$
(where $x$, $t$ and other values have S.I. units). The
dielectric constant of the medium is ______ .
(speed of light in free space is $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$)
questions.solution: Sol. $n = \frac{C}{V}$ $V = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{4.5 \times 10^{14}}{3 \times 10^6} = \frac{3}{2} \times 10^8$ $n = 2$ $n = \sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r} \quad (\mu_r = 1)$ $2 = \sqrt{\varepsilon_r}$ $\varepsilon_r = 4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A parallel beam of light travelling in air (refractive index $1.0$) is incident on a convex spherical glass surface of radius of curvature $50\text{ cm}$. Refractive index of glass is $1.5$. The rays converge to a point at a distance x cm from the centre of the curvature of the spherical surface. The value of x is ______ $\text{ cm}$.
questions.solution: Sol. A ray diagram showing parallel incident rays entering a convex refracting surface of radius $R=50$ and refractive index $\mu_2 = 1.5$ from a medium with refractive index $\mu_1 = 1$, converging to a point at a distance $v$ $$\frac{\mu_2}{\text{v}} - \frac{\mu_1}{\text{u}} = \frac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{\text{R}} \Rightarrow \frac{1.5}{\text{v}} - \frac{1}{\infty} = \frac{1.5 - 1}{50}$$ $\text{V} = 150 \text{ cm}$ $\text{x} \rightarrow \text{measure from center}$ $\text{x} = \text{V} - \text{R}$ $= 150 - 50 = 100 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A circular disc has radius $R_1$ and thickness $T_1$. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius $R_2$ and thickness $T_2$. If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = 2$ then $\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{1}{\alpha}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\underline{\quad\quad\quad}$.
questions.solution: Sol. Diagrams show two disks with parameters $(T_1, R_1)$ and $(T_2, R_2)$. $m_1 = \pi R_1^2 T_1 \rho \quad\quad\quad\quad\quad m_2 = \pi R_2^2 T_2 \rho$ $I_1 = \frac{m_1 R_1^2}{2} \quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad I_2 = \frac{m_2 R_2^2}{2}$ $I_1 = I_2$ $\frac{\pi R_1^2 T_1 \rho R_1^2}{2} = \frac{\pi R_2^2 T_2 \rho R_2^2}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{1}{16}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Inductance of a coil with $10^4$ turns is $10\text{ mH}$ and it is connected to a dc source of $10\text{ V}$ with internal resistance of $10\,\Omega$. The energy density in the inductor when the current reaches $\left(\frac{1}{\text{e}}\right)$ of its maximum value is $\alpha\pi \times \frac{1}{\text{e}^2}\text{ J/m}^3$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\text{\underline{\quad}}$. $(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ Tm/A})$.
questions.solution: Sol. $L = 10 \times 10^{-3} \text{ H}$ $N = 10^4$ Circuit diagram showing an inductor $L$, a resistor of $10\ \Omega$, and a cell of $10\text{ V}$ connected in a loop. $I_0 = \frac{10}{10} = 1\text{A}$ (max current) $I = \frac{1}{\text{e}}$ $E_{\text{d}} = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$ $B = \mu_0 \text{nI}$ $L = \mu_0 \text{n}^2\pi\text{R}^2\ell$ $E_{\text{d}} = \frac{\mu_0 \text{n}^2\text{I}^2}{2}$ $= \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^8 \times \frac{1}{\text{e}^2}}{2}$ $= \frac{20\pi}{\text{e}^2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the transition metal ions $\text{Mn}^{3+}$, $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ and $\text{Co}^{3+}$ and all form low spin octahedral complexes. The correct decreasing order of unpaired electrons in their respective d-orbitals of the complexes is
questions.solution: Sol. $\mathrm{Co}^{3+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{d}^6 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{2,2,2} \text{ } \mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0,0} \text{ ,unpaired electron} = 0$ $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{d}^5 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{2,2,1} \text{ } \mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0,0} \text{ unpaired electron} = 1$ $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{d}^3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{1,1,1} \text{ } \mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0,0} \text{ unpaired electron} = 3$ $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{d}^4 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{2,1,1} \text{ } \mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0,0} \text{ unpaired electron} = 2$
